# Feature: Sleeper — sanity check

<!-- Generated by the project-manager tool from pm.yml. Do not edit by hand; the store is the source of truth. -->

## Goal

Sanity-check candidate mechanic #33 (Sleeper) from Enemies and Bots before it is used in real levels. Effect: Sleeps until any orb is collected, then patrols a fixed loop. Unique: dormant until an orb pickup wakes it. Useful: collecting escalates danger, so orb order matters. Source status in the candidate file is 'revised'; it was revised from human review and is now treated as a trial candidate.

## User Story

**As a** player

**I want** sleeps until any orb is collected, then patrols a fixed loop.

**So that** collecting escalates danger, so orb order matters.

## High-Level Use Case

The player meets Sleeper for the first time in its teaching room (mech-33-sleeper-room). Teaching moment: First room: the nearest orb sits in front of a sleeping enemy, with a safer orb further away. A player who collects the nearest orb first wakes the sleeper across their return path and has to restart the room, which teaches that any orb can be the one that wakes it and that collection order is a decision. The sanity check plays that room, exercises every rule below, and records a replayable session.

## Player-Facing Behavior

- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: It sits asleep and solid on its tile (it blocks that tile) until any orb anywhere in the level is collected
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: It is not tied to one specific orb
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: From then on it patrols a fixed marked loop at one tile per player move, lethal on touch like a patroller

## Edge Cases & Rules

- It sits asleep and solid on its tile (it blocks that tile) until any orb anywhere in the level is collected
- Movement/state stays deterministic: state advances only through the pure step function with recorded t_ms; a recorded session replays to the same end state.
- Restart (R / restart) restores the room to its initial state, including this mechanic.

## UI / Feedback

- The player sees Sleeper's effect happen on its tile(s) exactly as the rules above describe; no hidden state.
- Any counter, inventory or HUD impact follows the rules above; if a rule needs a counter it is shown while it matters (see Open Questions).
- Failure in the teaching room returns the player to the room start / checkpoint for an immediate retry.

## Assets & Level Data Needed

- Level JSON: new Test Level mech-33-sleeper-room (rows + legend) implementing the teaching moment above.
- Sprites/defs: reuse existing tiles where the mechanic reuses an existing tile; add a new sprite/tile def only if this mechanic introduces a new tile (confirm in the implement task).
- Source: plans/level-design/candidate-mechanics/enemies-and-bots.yml mechanic #33.
